title: Learned symptom clusters track heart-failure emergency outcomes
summary: Fitted k-means partitioned nine recorded symptoms in438 emergency patients with prior heart failure into three groups. The indigestion group had adjusted odds ratios of1.8 for both acute heart-failure exacerbation and30-day adverse cardiac events compared with the group lacking indigestion and dyspnea. These are exploratory same-cohort associations, not a validated triage intervention.
organization: University of Pittsburgh; University of Pittsburgh Medical Center

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, reference definitions, model evaluation and Results independently read; no operational laboratory sections

evidence.ai_role: Fitted k-means learns symptom-based patient partitions; the resulting assignments enable clinical outcome comparisons. PCA performed poorly and was not the retained partition.
evidence.tested: A secondary analysis of prospectively collected emergency presentations used438 patients and nine binary symptoms. Silhouette analysis selected three clusters of178,100 and160 patients. Two reviewers adjudicated clinical outcomes; regression adjusted for selected baseline variables.
evidence.unknown: The same selected cohort was used to discover and test clusters, with univariate-informed adjustment. Confidence intervals for the reported odds ratios round to1.0; no independent replication or causal interpretation is established. Outcomes include a heterogeneous composite; clustering is not proof of distinct disease mechanisms or improved emergency decisions.
